plotEn:
In 1762, during the French and Indian War, two English families, the Clems and the Balfours, are on a ship headed to the Thirteen Colonies. As the ship arrives to shore, the French Navy ambushes them. Naval officer Nathaniel Clem is killed defending the ship's passengers as his youngest son Benjamin suffers a leg injury, forcing him to use a knee brace into adulthood.
Twelve years later in 1774, the Clems and Balfours have settled in Kingston, New York. Benjamin and his brother Jeremiah help their mother Rachel operate a grain mill. Jeremiah has his eyes set on Lord Balfour's daughter Elizabeth, maintaining a friendship with Balfour's young slave Emmalin, who has unrequited feelings for him. When news of the Battles of Lexington and Concord breaks out, the people of Kingston are split, with Benjamin expressing sympathy for the rebels. Jeremiah, having grown cynical and unwilling to disappoint Lord Balfour and Elizabeth, sides with the British Crown and joins the British Army, attempting to save face when Benjamin refuses to apologize for his dissent. Though the Clem brothers initially insist they will never be torn apart, they argue during Jeremiah's final supper at home before he joins a regiment led by Balfour.
